messages:
emma-cs: Heads-up: onboarding for Switchboard (acct switch-123) — their Go SDK init is getting 429s on preflight and /v1/generate. QA repros locally. :grimacing:
raj-dev: ugh, thanks. Can you paste the exact client config and a short log snippet?
emma-cs: sure — they use our go-sdk v0.9.2, parallel init from lambda warmup. snippet:
```
client, err := redwood.NewClient("sk-xxxx", redwood.WithRegion("us-west-2"), redwood.WithMaxParallelInit(40))
resp, err := client.Preflight(ctx, &redwood.PreflightReq{Iam: true})
```
logs: `preflight: 429 throttle, route=preflight, reason=rate_limit, retry_after=1s`
raj-dev: ok two suspects: 1) massively parallel preflight from many lambdas 2) ephemeral token refresh alignment. Did they use ephemeral creds per invocation?
emma-cs: yes per-invocation ephemeral tokens from their auth service, no splay, equal TTLs across hosts.
santiago-eng: pinging infra — if everyone refreshes near-simultaneously we'll see a thundering herd on our token validation /handshake. Also Go SDK MaxParallelInit=40 seems high for lambda coldstarts.
nova-support: deploy-bot: ticket created RW-12489 and assigned to onboarding-team.
raj-dev: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) reduce MaxParallelInit to 4–8, 2) add client-side jitter/splay on token refresh, 3) use short-lived shared warm pool for lambdas (reuse client across invocations).
emma-cs: sent that to customer — they asked for an immediate workaround while infra triages.
santiago-eng: also recommend enabling preflight coalescing on their tenant (we can flip a flag for 24h) and temporary rate-increase window for onboarding.
emma-cs: customer accepted: lowered parallel to 6, added exponential backoff + jitter, and we toggled preflight coalescing.
raj-dev: follow-up: add note to onboarding checklist about default MaxParallelInit and ephemeral token splay. I'll open a docs PR.
emma-cs: thanks — will close after 24h observation. tagging @santiago-eng for any infra followups. :thumbsup:
